name: Dismantlable Ample Classes Are Preserved by Two-Sided Dismantlable Tests
statement: If the outer class $C$, a proper nonempty test $T$, and its cube complement $T^{\mathrm c}$ all have ordering width zero, then $C\circ_iT$ has width zero. Thus $T$ preserves every dismantlable ample outer class exactly when both test sides are dismantlable ample. If both exclusive outer sections are nonempty, then for the individual substitution $\sigma(C\circ_iT)=0$ exactly when $\sigma(C)=\sigma(T)=\sigma(T^{\mathrm c})=0$.
proof: Process a zero-width outer order in blocks. In the first block at an outside word use the relevant test-side order forward; after the opposite block is complete, use the reverse-complement filling order. Inner predecessors then supply an earlier inner neighbor. For a predecessor in a completed outer block, the outer zero-cost witness either changes an outside coordinate, preserving the inner word, or crosses the distinguished coordinate, in which case the completed opposite inner block supplies a neighbor. For necessity, singleton outer classes recover each test side; when both exclusive sections occur, a crossing test edge recovers $C$ and exclusive outside words recover both test sides by conditioning.
